sources.cite: National POLST. National POLST Form (copyright May 2025)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes: Section A applies when the patient 'has no pulse and is not breathing' (NO CPR: 'Do Not Attempt Resuscitation'); Section B applies when the patient 'has a pulse and/or is breathing'; Selective Treatments: 'Attempt to restore function while avoiding intensive care if possible (e.g., ventilator, defibrillation)', 'May use non-invasive positive airway pressure, antibiotics and IV fluids as indicated', 'Transfer to hospital if treatment needs cannot be met in current location'; Comfort-Focused: 'Maximize comfort through symptom management; allow natural death'. 'This form does not expire.' States use their own versions.

sources.cite: NASEMSO. National Model EMS Clinical Guidelines, Version 3.0 (March 2022): Do Not Resuscitate Status/Advance Directives/Healthcare Power of Attorney Status
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in the full text Iowa HHS hosts (https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/198/download) through summarizing fetches with quotes; NASEMSO's own page, read the same day, still presents Version 3 (2022) as current and names no later version. A patient with a valid exclusion who has signs of life 'should receive full treatment per protocols with the exception of any intervention specifically prohibited'; a POLST 'may provide specific guidance'; 'Directives should be followed as closely as possible and medical direction contacted as needed'; if a prohibited intervention is being considered, contact medical direction; a document whose validity is in question: resuscitate until more is known.

sources.cite: NASEMSO. National Model EMS Clinical Guidelines, Version 3.0 (March 2022): Respiratory Distress (Includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema); Airway Management
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in the full text Iowa HHS hosts (https://hhs.iowa.gov/media/198/download) through summarizing fetches with quotes; NASEMSO's own page, read the same day, still presents Version 3 (2022) as current and names no later version. Albuterol nebulized for bronchospasm, repeated for ongoing distress; noninvasive ventilation (CPAP) for severe distress, considered early; start PEEP at 5 cmH2O and raise in 2-3 cmH2O steps to the lowest effective pressure; if the patient worsens on CPAP (worse mental status, rising EtCO2, vomiting), 'remove CPAP/BiPAP and escalate airway management options'; target SpO2 94-98%, and 'permissive hypoxia (SPO2 >= 90%) may be appropriate in patients with COPD'; avoid nitrates within 48 hours of a phosphodiesterase inhibitor. The guideline's albuterol dose for distress (5 mg) is above the inhalation solution's labeled 2.5 mg; the case uses the labeled 2.5 mg dose, repeated.

sources.cite: NHTSA. National EMS Scope of Practice Model 2019: Including Change Notices 1.0 and 2.0 (DOT HS 813 151, 2021-08-01)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17: the record page (title, report number, date; the change notices add intramuscular injection, vaccination in a public health emergency and nasal swab collection at EMT and above) and the PDF's skill tables through a summarizing fetch whose table columns were partly unclear, so placement was checked against the course's own reading (backend/supabase/seed/labs/ems-sources.ts, 2026-11-09) and REQ-241's reading (2026-11-11). EMR: oxygen, BVM, naloxone (intranasal or auto-injector), unit-dose hazmat antidote auto-injectors, tourniquet, wound packing, emergency moves, manual stabilization; no pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring or transport. EMT adds pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring, oral glucose, aspirin, the patient's own nitroglycerin, an inhaled bronchodilator, CPAP, the epinephrine auto-injector. AEMT adds IV and IO access, non-medicated IV fluids, supraglottic airways, waveform capnography, sublingual nitroglycerin and a limited list of IV and IM drugs (dextrose, naloxone). Paramedic adds 12-lead interpretation, manual defibrillation, synchronized cardioversion, transcutaneous pacing, needle chest decompression, intubation and medicated infusions. No newer model was found on 2026-11-17.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

His breathing as one severity score: untreated it climbs about 0.015 a minute; oxygen alone slows it, CPAP reverses it at about 0.02 a minute. Authored FLAG figures. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

brief.situation: 11:40. You are a paramedic with an EMT partner. Henry, 88, has advanced dementia and COPD; his son, who is his health care agent, called because Henry is breathing hard since last night. A POLST form is on the refrigerator. His daughter has just arrived from out of town.
handover: Henry cannot take part in decisions. His son is his legal health care agent and is on the phone, on his way.
You carry oxygen, CPAP, nebulized albuterol, IV supplies and intubation equipment. Online medical direction is a radio call away. The hospital is 15 minutes away.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated seconds per real second. Pause any time.
Every assessment and treatment takes the time it would on a real call. Scene time and the drive run on the clock.
Partway through you are asked to explain your decisions in writing. The case ends when care is handed over, then a debrief scores what you did.

safetyNote: Teaching case for exam practice; fictional patient. Not medical advice; follow your local protocols and medical direction.

why.question: His daughter asked you to do everything. What does the POLST let you do, and how did you handle the disagreement?

parts.label: What the POLST says
parts.criteria: A valid POLST (his name, signatures, intact): Section A NO CPR applies only if pulseless and not breathing; with a pulse, Section B Selective Treatments applies: CPAP, IV fluids, antibiotics and transfer are allowed; intubation and intensive care are not. DNR does not mean no treatment.
parts.modelAnswer: The POLST is valid. He has a pulse and is breathing, so Section B applies: Selective Treatments. CPAP and transport are allowed; intubation is not. 'No CPR' only matters if he arrests.

parts.label: The disagreement
parts.criteria: Follow the patient's documented wishes; explain them compassionately to the daughter; the son is the legal agent; contact medical direction when a prohibited intervention is being requested.
parts.modelAnswer: I explained the form was Henry's own choice, kept caring for him, and called medical direction because a prohibited intervention was being requested; his son, the legal agent, agreed.

honored.headline: DNR is not 'do not treat'
honored.body: With a pulse, Section B governs: CPAP and transport, no ventilator. His wishes, kindly explained, and medical direction for the disagreement.

arrived.headline: Arrived, with gaps
arrived.body: Check how soon CPAP went on, and whether his daughter and medical direction were involved.

intubated.headline: He declined a ventilator
intubated.body: A valid POLST with Selective Treatments rules out intubation. A family member's request does not override it; call medical direction.

withheld.headline: DNR is about CPR
withheld.body: Section A applies only without a pulse. His form allowed CPAP and transport; withholding them was not his wish.

scoring.modelReasoning: Read and validate the POLST (his name, signatures, intact). Section A (NO CPR) applies only if he is pulseless and not breathing; with a pulse, Section B Selective Treatments governs: noninvasive positive airway pressure, IV fluids, antibiotics and transfer are allowed, a ventilator is not. So: CPAP, albuterol, transport, no intubation. Explain the form kindly to his daughter; his son is the legal agent; call medical direction because a prohibited intervention is being requested (NASEMSO). Send the POLST with him and notify.

secB.ask: While you read the form: Henry has a pulse and is breathing. Which section tells you what to do now?
secB.explain: National POLST: Section A applies when the patient has no pulse and is not breathing; Section B when the patient has a pulse and/or is breathing.
